title: U.S. House, District 6
what_it_does: Represents Florida's 6th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives; votes on federal laws and spending.
verified_ballot_note: UPDATE (Sept 2026 research pass): Ballotpedia's general-election listing (search snippet) shows Christopher Manuel Alcantara and Amr Metwally both running with No Party Affiliation on Nov. 3, 2026 alongside Randy Fine (R) and Eric Yonce (D) (https://ballotpedia.org/Florida's_6th_Congressional_District_election,_2026). News4Jax voter guide and Ballotpedia snippet: incumbent Randy Fine (R) and Eric Yonce (D) won their Aug. 18, 2026 primaries; Ballotpedia snippet also lists Christopher Manuel Alcantara and Amr Metwally as general-election candidates (party affiliation not shown in the snippet; recorded here as No Party Affiliation pending verification) (https://www.news4jax.com/voters-guide/2026/07/31/2026-voters-guide-floridas-6th-congressional-district/ ; https://ballotpedia.org/Florida's_6th_Congressional_District_election,_2026). Fine's primary vote share was not reliably found (one snippet's percentages appeared to reference a different race and were not used). Florida's Legislature passed a new congressional map in the April 2026 special session (Senate vote 21-17 on April 29, 2026) and the Florida Supreme Court on June 10, 2026 declined (6-1) to block it, so the new district lines apply to the Nov. 3, 2026 election; litigation on the merits continues. (https://floridaphoenix.com/2026/04/29/florida-legislature-passes-desantis-congressional-redistricting-map/; https://mynews13.com/fl/orlando/news/2026/06/10/florida-supreme-court-clears-way-for-new-redistricting-map-in-2026; https://www.wusf.org/politics-issues/2026-06-11/florida-supreme-court-rejects-challenge-new-redistricting-map) County list reflects pre-2026 district boundaries unless a 2026 source is cited; boundaries changed under the April 2026 map and the exact new county composition was not confirmed in searches run for this guide.

candidates.name: Randy Fine
candidates.photo_source: Official congressional portrait (unitedstates.github.io mirror of the Congressional Pictorial Directory; downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: U.S. Representative (since April 2025); former Florida state senator
candidates.residence: Melbourne Beach/Palm Bay area, Brevard County (per prior reporting; not re-verified)
candidates.background: Randy Fine, described by FOX 35 as a Harvard graduate and business executive, served in the Florida House (2016-2024) and Florida Senate (2024-2025) before winning the April 1, 2025 special election to replace Michael Waltz in the 6th District, with President Trump's endorsement. In the Florida House he sponsored the 2023 universal school-voucher expansion. He won the Aug. 18, 2026 Republican primary over Ernest Audino, Charles Gambaro and Alexandra van Cleef (vote share not reliably found) and faces Democrat Eric Yonce plus two no-party candidates in November. In Congress he voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act and the SAVE Act and opposed the June 2026 Ukraine aid bill.

candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Real-estate professional and small-business owner (vintage Airstream remodeling); former big-box retail manager and former Ocala Police Department employee

candidates.background: Eric Yonce grew up in Citra in Marion County and graduated from North Marion High School; his father was an Ocala police officer. He worked for the Ocala Police Department, earned a business degree, spent more than 20 years managing big-box retail stores, and now works in real estate and runs a small business remodeling vintage Airstream trailers (Florida Politics; campaign site). He won the Aug. 18, 2026 Democratic primary with 32% over Ronnie Murchinson-Rivera, Steve Morgan and Rob Cooper and faces Rep. Randy Fine in November. His platform emphasizes coastal protection, affordable housing, health-care affordability and immigration reform.

candidates.background: Andrew Parrott is the Libertarian candidate in Florida's 6th Congressional District. He is 54, married, a welder and entrepreneur and a graduate of the Aviation Institute of Maintenance. He ran for the same seat in the April 2025 special election and says he is not beholden to either major party.

candidates.name: Alec Pavlik
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Write-in candidate: the name is not printed on the ballot; voters must write it on the blank line
candidates.background: Alec Pavlik is a write-in candidate in Florida's 6th Congressional District who says he grew up in the district and has lived there his whole life. His campaign is built on what he calls constitutionalism: he says members of Congress have voted for bills that violate the Constitution and pledges to vote against such measures and to work to repeal past ones.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

taxes.summary: Pavlik says inflation can only be eliminated if Congress passes balanced budgets and returns to what he calls sound money, and argues government has no authority to create taxes or welfare that benefit one class of people rather than the general public.
taxes.quote: Inflation can only be eliminated if Congress passes balanced budgets and the United States returns to sound money.

sources.title: Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey: Alec Pavlik (completed 2025; read 2026-09-21)

ukraine.summary: Pavlik argues that aid to foreign countries should come voluntarily from people rather than through government, saying that if Americans want to help a foreign land they will do so, often more efficiently, without government coercion.
ukraine.quote: If the People want to provide aid to a foreign land, a neighbor, or a company, they will (and often more efficiently) without the coercion of government.

sources.title: Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey: Alec Pavlik (completed 2025; read 2026-09-21)

guns.summary: In his 2025 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, Pavlik described self-defense as a natural right that government has no authority to infringe, and named firearm policy as one of the areas he is personally passionate about because it affects natural rights.
guns.quote: Some of these rights include the right to life, liberty, property, self-defense, and the pursuit of happiness. Governments are established to provide security for these rights.

sources.title: Alec Pavlik - Ballotpedia (2025 Candidate Connection survey)

other_issues.title: Constitutional government and natural rights
other_issues.summary: Pavlik says Congress must reclaim all federal legislative power from the executive and unelected officials, and that rights including life, liberty, property and self-defense are inherent and government exists to secure them.
